Metadata.title: ATELIER — Architecture & Living
Metadata.description: A fictional contemporary architecture studio — a frontend portfolio project.

Home.heroText: ATELIER is a fictional studio designing homes, workplaces and public rooms around light, material and the quiet of well-judged space.
Home.heroCaption: Sample illustration: placeholder artwork for a fictional studio.
Home.studioText1: We believe good architecture is mostly attention: to the sun on a wall at four in the afternoon, to the way a hand meets a door, to what a building will need in fifty years.
Home.studioText2: Our small team works across homes, workplaces and cultural rooms, drawing every project from the site outwards and building it from materials that age well.
Home.valueLightText: Plans and sections are shaped by how daylight moves through the day.
Home.valueMaterialText: Timber, lime, stone and brick, left to show how they are made.
Home.valueLongevityText: Details that are easy to repair and buildings that can change use.
Home.statsNote: Figures are drawn from this demo's sample data, not from a real practice.
Home.ctaText: Tell us about the plot, the brief or just the feeling you are after. The form on the contact page is a demo, but it shows how the conversation would start.

Services.metaDescription: Residential, villa, interior, commercial, renovation, sustainable and concept design from a fictional architecture studio.
Services.title: From first sketch to the last joint.
Services.intro: Seven areas of practice, each with a clear way of working. Every service below shows how we usually approach it and the sample projects that relate to it.

residential.title: Residential architecture
residential.summary: Homes shaped around daily routines, orientation and the way light moves through a day.
residential.description: From single-family houses to small apartment buildings, we start with how people actually live and let the plan, section and openings follow.
residential.step1Text: A brief built from your routines, site walks and a short list of non-negotiables.
residential.step2Text: Plans and sections tested in physical and digital models until the rooms feel right.
residential.step3Text: Detailed drawings and site visits so the finished house matches the intent.

villa.title: Villa design
villa.summary: Larger houses and retreats where landscape, privacy and craft carry as much weight as the plan.
villa.description: Villas ask for a clear relationship to terrain and climate. We design buildings and outdoor rooms together, from entry sequence to material palette.
villa.step1Text: Sun, wind, views and drainage are mapped before the first line is drawn.
villa.step2Text: Volumes, courtyards and terraces are arranged to frame views and protect privacy.
villa.step3Text: Joinery, stone and planting schedules are specified as part of the architecture.

interior.title: Interior design
interior.summary: Rooms resolved down to the joint: natural timber, lime, stone and light-led layouts.
interior.description: We design interiors as part of the building, not a coat of paint over it. Furniture, lighting and surfaces are chosen as one system.
interior.step1Text: Use, mood and budget are agreed through a concise interior brief.
interior.step2Text: Layouts, material boards and lighting studies are reviewed together.
interior.step3Text: Bespoke pieces are detailed, procured and checked on site.

commercial.title: Commercial spaces
commercial.summary: Offices, studios and retail spaces that are flexible, legible and pleasant to work in.
commercial.description: Workplaces change faster than buildings. We plan structure and services to allow reconfiguration while keeping daylight, acoustics and circulation right.
commercial.step1Text: Teams, growth and ways of working are translated into a space programme.
commercial.step2Text: Layout options are compared against daylight, acoustics and circulation.
commercial.step3Text: Phased drawings and coordination keep the project on programme.

renovation.title: Renovation
renovation.summary: Careful reuse of existing buildings, keeping what has character and fixing what does not.
renovation.description: Old structures hold embodied energy and stories. We survey, repair and reinterpret them so new use sits comfortably inside old walls.
renovation.step1Text: Measured drawings and condition surveys reveal what the building can carry.
renovation.step2Text: We agree what to keep, repair or replace, and why.
renovation.step3Text: Repairs and interventions are detailed to be honest about old and new.

sustainable.title: Sustainable design
sustainable.summary: Passive strategies first: orientation, shading, thermal mass and low-carbon materials.
sustainable.description: Sustainability is decided in the earliest sketches, not added at the end. We prioritise passive performance, durable materials and buildings that are easy to repair.
sustainable.step1Text: Early energy and daylight studies steer form and orientation.
sustainable.step2Text: Materials are chosen for durability, repairability and embodied carbon.
sustainable.step3Text: Performance is checked against targets as drawings develop.

concept.title: Concept design
concept.summary: A focused early phase that turns a site and an ambition into a clear architectural idea.
concept.description: Not every project needs the full journey straight away. Concept design gives you a defined idea, massing studies and a realistic direction before you commit further.
concept.step1Text: Site, regulations and references are gathered into a short study.
concept.step2Text: Several directions are drawn quickly and compared openly.
concept.step3Text: One concept is developed into a presentation you can build on.
